approvalRequirements: Be a current or new Southwest Gas residential customer at a qualifying Nevada service address.
Purchase and install a qualifying solar water-heating system that uses natural gas as the backup water-heating fuel and meets current equipment specifications.
Use a Southwest Gas Program Qualified Contractor, who must support and sign the rebate submission.
Submit the completed application with invoices, equipment certifications, installation records, permits, and other required supporting documents.
Allow any requested inspection, measurement, or verification and apply while program funds remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Southwest Gas maintains an administrative solar water-heating rebate pathway for qualifying Nevada systems installed by Program Qualified Contractors. A complete compliant claim is likely to be paid after review while funds remain available.
reviews.evidenceText: Current Southwest Gas materials state that qualifying solar water-heating systems with natural-gas backup may receive rebates and that Nevada program systems must be installed by Program Qualified Contractors who facilitate applications and verification.

approvalRequirements: Own taxable property that is part of a qualifying wind power project in West Virginia.
Limit the special valuation to qualifying wind turbines, towers, and associated pollution-control personal property covered by the statute.
Report the property through the normal annual property-tax assessment process and provide information needed for the Tax Commissioner to allocate qualifying value.
Accept that other project property remains subject to ordinary assessment and that the qualifying allocation may not exceed the statutory percentage.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The special valuation is prescribed by West Virginia statute rather than awarded competitively. Qualifying wind-project components should receive the statutory assessment treatment when properly reported and allocated.
reviews.evidenceText: West Virginia law classifies qualifying wind-project turbines and towers as pollution-control property valued at salvage value, subject to Tax Commissioner allocation and a statutory cap on the qualifying share of facility value.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Spire Missouri commercial or industrial natural-gas customer at the installation address.
Select equipment or a project that qualifies under Spire's current business rebate specifications.
Obtain any measure-specific or custom-project preapproval required before purchase or installation.
Use an appropriately licensed or certified contractor and install the approved qualifying equipment.
Submit the business rebate application with the account, invoice, manufacturer, full model number, purchase date, installation date, and contractor verification.
Complete any inspection or additional documentation requested by Spire.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Spire publishes objective business rebate criteria and documentation requirements. Prescriptive claims that meet customer, equipment, contractor, and filing rules are likely to be approved, while custom projects depend on required preapproval and savings review.
reviews.evidenceText: Spire's current business and application-guide pages require qualifying natural-gas equipment, a licensed or certified contractor, the correct Missouri program information, itemized proof of purchase, full model data, installation dates, and contractor verification.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Spire Missouri residential natural-gas customer at the installation address.
Purchase and install currently qualifying natural-gas heating or water-heating equipment that meets the published efficiency specifications.
Use an appropriately licensed contractor; unlicensed installations are not processable under the current guide.
Submit the correct Missouri offer code, account and service-address information, receipt or invoice, manufacturer, full model number, purchase date, installation date, and contractor verification.
Respond to any request for clarification or installation verification and apply within the current program period.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current residential program uses published equipment and documentation criteria rather than competitive selection. A timely complete claim for eligible natural-gas equipment is likely to be paid; ordinary electric heat-pump equipment is not established by the cited gas-rebate materials.
reviews.evidenceText: Spire currently directs residential customers to equipment-specific rebates and requires the correct account and offer information, qualifying equipment, licensed installation, itemized purchase records, full model details, installation dates, and contractor verification.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Spire Missouri residential natural-gas customer at the installation address.
Purchase and install a currently qualifying high-efficiency natural-gas furnace or other listed heating measure.
Use an appropriately licensed contractor and satisfy all published equipment and installation specifications.
Submit the correct Missouri rebate application with account information, itemized invoice or receipt, manufacturer, full model number, purchase date, installation date, and contractor verification.
Complete any requested review or verification within the current filing period.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: This is an objective equipment-rebate process. An eligible Spire Missouri customer with qualifying high-efficiency gas heating equipment, licensed installation, and complete documentation is likely to receive the published rebate after administrative review.
reviews.evidenceText: Current Spire guidance requires qualifying residential natural-gas equipment, licensed installation, correct Missouri offer and account information, itemized proof of purchase, full model data, installation dates, and contractor verification.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Spire Missouri commercial or industrial natural-gas customer at the installation address.
Select equipment or a project that qualifies under Spire's current business rebate specifications.
Obtain any required preapproval for custom or measure-specific projects before committing to the work.
Use an appropriately licensed or certified contractor and complete the qualifying installation.
Submit the application with account information, itemized invoices, manufacturer and full model data, purchase and installation dates, and contractor verification.
Pass any requested inspection or technical verification.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Spire's current commercial pathway is documentation-based and uses published criteria. A qualifying prescriptive project is likely to be paid after review, while custom measures remain contingent on preapproval and verified savings.
reviews.evidenceText: Spire currently requires qualifying business equipment, licensed or certified installation, the correct Missouri program information, itemized purchase records, full model data, installation dates, contractor verification, and any applicable project review.

approvalRequirements: Be a qualifying Spring Valley Public Utilities business customer at the project location.
Use the applicable 2026 business rebate form and install equipment that meets its measure-specific technical requirements.
Obtain preapproval when required for custom, industrial, or other non-prescriptive work.
Submit the completed form with invoices or receipts, equipment model and specification information, installation details, and any savings calculations required by the form.
Allow Spring Valley Public Utilities or its program representative to verify the project and apply while rebate funding remains available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Spring Valley publishes current 2026 forms for lighting, HVAC, refrigeration, food service, motors, compressed air, and custom measures. A conforming prescriptive claim is likely to be approved after routine review, subject to any required custom preapproval and available funds.
reviews.evidenceText: The current Spring Valley page provides 2026 business rebate forms for lighting, HVAC, refrigeration, food service, motors, compressed air, controls, and custom projects, establishing a current application and review pathway.

approvalRequirements: Be a qualifying Spring Valley Public Utilities residential customer at the installation address.
Purchase and install equipment covered by a current 2026 residential rebate form and meet the form's efficiency and installation specifications.
Submit the applicable completed form with receipts or invoices, equipment model information, and installation documentation.
Complete any utility verification requested and apply within the current program period while funds remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Spring Valley maintains current 2026 residential forms for qualifying ENERGY STAR products, cooling equipment, heat-pump-related measures, motors, and other listed products. Complete claims meeting the form criteria are likely to be paid after administrative review.
reviews.evidenceText: The current Spring Valley page lists 2026 residential rebate applications for ENERGY STAR products, cooling equipment, EV chargers, circulator pumps, furnace fan motors, pool pumps, and aerosol sealing.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Springfield Utility Board commercial, industrial, or public electric customer.
Contact SUB and obtain project prequalification or written preapproval before purchasing equipment or starting the project.
Provide project, baseline, equipment, operating, cost, and savings information needed for SUB's technical review or energy audit.
Install the approved qualifying scope in accordance with SUB's conditions.
Submit final invoices and technical records and pass any post-installation verification required before payment.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: SUB expressly offers incentives for eligible pre-qualified projects. A project that receives preapproval, follows the approved scope, and supplies complete closeout records is likely to receive the incentive after verification.
reviews.evidenceText: SUB's current business materials state that energy-efficiency upgrades must be eligible and pre-qualified, and the commercial incentive form states that preapproval is required for project eligibility.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Springfield Utility Board residential electric customer at the property receiving the improvement.
Select a currently financeable residential efficiency measure and complete any required SUB energy assessment before installation.
Submit the loan application and project or contractor information before work begins.
Pass SUB's credit, account-history, and loan-amount review and receive approval before committing to the project.
Complete the approved installation, provide final invoices and documentation, allow verification, and execute the loan documents.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current zero-interest loan options have defined eligible measures, but financing is not automatic. Approval depends on customer and property eligibility, energy review, credit or account history, project approval, and final documentation.
reviews.evidenceText: SUB currently offers zero-interest residential loans for qualifying heat pumps, insulation, windows, and other measures. Current pages require measure-specific eligibility and energy review, and direct customers to obtain and complete a loan application before funding.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Springfield Utility Board residential electric customer at the installation address.
Choose a currently rebated measure and satisfy its equipment, property, contractor, and installation requirements.
Complete any required energy assessment, sizing review, or preauthorization before installation.
Submit the measure-specific application with receipts or invoices, equipment model and efficiency data, contractor information, and other required records.
Allow SUB to inspect or otherwise verify the completed project before payment.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: SUB publishes current measure-specific residential rebates with objective requirements. A customer that completes required prequalification, installs eligible equipment, and submits a complete claim is likely to receive payment after review.
reviews.evidenceText: SUB currently lists residential rebates for heat pumps, heat-pump water heaters, insulation, smart thermostats, EV chargers, windows, and related measures, with measure-specific applications and eligibility review.

approvalRequirements: Have a solar facility or proposed project that qualifies for an available Delaware SREC procurement tier.
Obtain or maintain required Delaware Public Service Commission renewable-energy certification and provide complete system or project information.
Submit a bid through the procurement portal during the annual two-week application window and provide any required bid deposit.
Pass administrative bid validation and rank among the lowest valid bids accepted until the applicable tier capacity is filled.
Execute the procurement contract and satisfy project-completion, metering, reporting, and delivery obligations.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: This is a competitive procurement rather than an entitlement. Valid applications are ranked by bid price within limited tier capacity, and no open 2026 application window was verified on the current site as of the audit date.
reviews.evidenceText: The current Delaware SREC site describes an annual two-week bid window, administrative validation, and selection of the lowest valid bids by tier until procurement capacity is filled. The posted 2025 procurement is closed, and a current 2026 round was not posted.

approvalRequirements: Be a qualifying permanent SRP residential electric customer at the installation address.
Purchase and install a currently listed measure that meets the applicable efficiency, replacement, equipment, and property requirements.
Use an Arizona-licensed contractor or plumber where the measure rules require one.
Complete installation during the current eligibility period and submit the claim within the measure-specific deadline.
Provide the signed application, itemized invoice or receipt, manufacturer and model data, contractor information, and any other required supporting records.
Allow SRP to inspect or verify the installation if requested.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: SRP publishes fixed residential rebate amounts and objective measure criteria. A qualifying customer with compliant equipment, timely documentation, and any required licensed installation is likely to receive payment after administrative review.
reviews.evidenceText: Current SRP pages list residential incentives for qualifying air-conditioning, heat-pump water-heating, EV charging, and other measures, with customer, equipment, licensed-installer, filing-deadline, documentation, and inspection requirements.

approvalRequirements: Use the dwelling as an eligible Oregon primary residence.
Use fuel oil or dyed diesel from an eligible fuel dealer as the residence's primary heating fuel when applying and after the project is completed.
Complete an eligible weatherization measure that meets the current minimum-value requirements and does not discontinue use of the eligible dealer fuel.
Pay for the completed work and submit the cash-payment application within one year of completion.
Provide proof of eligible fuel purchases, paid receipts or itemized invoices, and income documentation when seeking the Tier 1 payment level.
Apply while first-come program funding remains available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: SHOW uses published customer, fuel, measure, documentation, and timing rules and processes payments first-come. A complete application for an eligible weatherization project is likely to be approved while funds remain.
reviews.evidenceText: Oregon's current SHOW pages require a primary Oregon residence heated by eligible dealer fuel, qualifying weatherization work, continued use of that fuel, paid project records, fuel-purchase proof, timely filing, and income records for the higher payment tier.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible nonresidential customer of a participating California investor-owned utility.
Purchase a qualifying high-efficiency commercial water-heating product covered by the current program.
Buy through a participating distributor that can validate the customer, utility territory, product, and rebate eligibility.
Provide the distributor with the customer and installation information needed to apply the instant point-of-sale rebate.
Install and use the qualifying water-heating product at the eligible commercial site in accordance with program rules.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current program is active, but its official scope is qualifying commercial water-heating equipment. The sole mapped retrofit in this record is high-efficiency HVAC replacement, which is outside the substantiated program scope.
reviews.evidenceText: The current statewide midstream program provides point-of-sale rebates for qualifying high-efficiency commercial water-heating products purchased through participating distributors by eligible customers of California investor-owned utilities; it does not substantiate general HVAC replacement rebates.

approvalRequirements: Be a Stearns Electric Association member or install the project at a site where Stearns supplies electricity.
Purchase qualifying new commercial, industrial, or agricultural equipment on or after January 1, 2026 and meet the applicable technical specifications.
Complete any measure-specific calculation, contractor, or installation requirements in the current rebate form.
Submit the completed application with the purchase receipt or itemized invoice, equipment model and specification data, and installation information.
Allow program verification and apply while limited first-come rebate funds remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Stearns publishes current 2026 prescriptive business rebates for the mapped lighting, HVAC, refrigeration, drives, charging, and related measures. A complete compliant claim is likely to be paid after routine review while funds remain.
reviews.evidenceText: Stearns Electric's current 2026 business page lists rebates for lighting retrofits, refrigeration, compressed air, EC motors and drives, food service, electric forklifts and charging, HVAC, and related equipment, with applications, receipts, specifications, and limited funding.

approvalRequirements: Be a Stearns Electric Association member and propose work at an eligible home, business, or agricultural building that is at least one year old.
Use loan proceeds for an improvement on Stearns Electric's current qualifying energy-improvement list or obtain written confirmation that an unlisted measure is eligible.
Submit the Energy Resource Conservation loan application with project cost and contractor or vendor information.
Pass Stearns Electric's review of the member's payment history and the requested loan amount and term.
Accept the approved loan terms and complete the project in accordance with the loan agreement.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current loan program is available for listed efficiency improvements, but battery storage—the only mapped retrofit for this record—is not identified on the current eligible-measure list. Financing would require separate written confirmation or a program change.
reviews.evidenceText: Stearns Electric currently offers member efficiency loans for specified heating, water-heating, weatherization, window, door, fan, and related improvements, subject to an application and payment-history review. Battery storage is not listed among the published qualifying improvements.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Stearns Electric Association residential member at the installation address.
Purchase and install equipment covered by a current ENERGY STAR or EnergyWise residential rebate and meet the published efficiency requirements.
Enroll the equipment in any required load-control or off-peak program and permit utility checkout where the specific measure requires it.
Submit the applicable rebate application with the receipt or invoice, manufacturer and model information, installation details, and contractor documentation.
Apply while limited first-come rebate funding remains available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Stearns maintains current prescriptive residential rebates with published equipment and documentation rules. An eligible member with a qualifying installation and complete claim is likely to receive payment, subject to any required load-control enrollment and available funds.
reviews.evidenceText: Stearns Electric currently publishes residential ENERGY STAR and EnergyWise rebates for qualifying appliances, heat pumps, geothermal systems, water heating, controls, and related equipment, with applications, purchase records, program enrollment where applicable, and limited funding.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Stowe Electric customer with an active account.
Purchase or lease a qualifying new or used battery-electric or plug-in hybrid vehicle under the current 2026 program.
Submit the signed 2026 rebate application after the purchase or lease.
Provide proof of purchase or lease, Vermont registration, vehicle identification and model information, and other requested customer records.
Provide income documentation only when requesting an enhanced income-qualified rebate and authorize program verification.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Stowe Electric publishes a current after-purchase vehicle rebate form with objective customer, vehicle, registration, and documentation requirements. A complete qualifying vehicle claim is likely to be approved; charger installation is addressed by separate Stowe Electric programs.
reviews.evidenceText: Stowe Electric's current electric-vehicle page provides a 2026 after-purchase rebate form requiring customer and vehicle information, purchase or lease proof, Vermont registration, and additional income records only for enhanced incentives.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Stowe Electric customer or project host within the utility's service area.
Install qualifying Level 2 or DC fast-charging equipment at an eligible multifamily, workplace, commercial, or public location.
Coordinate with Stowe Electric before installation when service, capacity, siting, or program confirmation is required.
Meet public-access, networking, operations, maintenance, and payment-portal requirements applicable to the charger type.
Submit the current 2026 rebate form with proof of purchase and installation, equipment specifications, site information, and requested supporting records.
Allow installation verification before payment.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Stowe Electric maintains a current public charging rebate pathway for qualifying Level 2 and DC fast chargers. A compliant installation with the required site, networking, documentation, and verification is likely to receive the published incentive.
reviews.evidenceText: The current Stowe Electric page offers 2026 rebates for Level 2 charging at multifamily, workplace, and public sites and for public DC fast charging, with equipment, access, networking, application, and verification conditions.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Sulphur Springs Valley Electric Cooperative member at the installation address.
Purchase and install a qualifying heat pump or other currently listed measure that meets the published efficiency and configuration requirements.
Satisfy measure-specific controls, contractor certification, and installation requirements, including dual-fuel conditions where applicable.
Submit the completed rebate form with the contractor signature, receipt or invoice, manufacturer and model information, and installation data within the current filing deadline.
Allow SSVEC to review or verify the installation.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: SSVEC publishes fixed heat-pump rebates and objective equipment and filing rules. A qualifying member installation with a complete application submitted within the stated period is likely to be paid after review.
reviews.evidenceText: SSVEC's current pages publish heat-pump rebate amounts, efficiency and dual-fuel requirements, contractor and invoice documentation, a filing deadline after installation, and a separate no-cost energy-audit service.

approvalRequirements: Have an eligible existing home in a participating Summit County jurisdiction.
Enroll in HC3's Energy Smart Colorado program and schedule a call with an HC3 Energy Coach before seeking a rebate.
Complete a home energy assessment before applying when the selected project is marked as requiring one.
Meet the applicable project, equipment, contractor, residency, and income-documentation rules for the home's jurisdiction and rebate tier.
Submit the online rebate application within 90 days of the paid invoice with final invoices or receipts, completion photos, and applicable specification sheets.
Allow post-project inspection and apply while limited first-come funding remains available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: HC3's 2026 program uses published jurisdiction, project, documentation, and timing rules rather than competitive scoring. A properly enrolled household with a qualifying completed project is likely to receive the rebate while first-come funds remain.
reviews.evidenceText: HC3's current 2026 requirements make rebates available first-come throughout Summit County, require Energy Smart enrollment and an Energy Coach call, specify assessment and project rules, and require an online application with invoices, photos, and specifications within 90 days.

approvalRequirements: Be an Arkansas state agency, board, or commission proposing work in a qualifying state-owned building.
Propose a renovation that fits the Sustainable Building Design Revolving Loan Fund's state-building purpose.
Provide the Division of Building Authority with the project scope, estimated costs, expected benefits or savings, implementation schedule, and other information it requires.
Receive Division of Building Authority project and financing approval before loan funds are committed.
Execute the loan and repayment documents and comply with project, reporting, and closeout conditions.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current official source confirms a revolving loan fund for renovations of state-owned buildings, but funding is not an automatic rebate and depends on project-specific approval and financing terms. Non-state-owned property is outside the current substantiated scope.
reviews.evidenceText: The Arkansas Division of Building Authority currently identifies itself as manager of the Sustainable Building Design Revolving Loan Fund for renovations of state-owned buildings and states that it does not oversee residential, commercial, city, or municipal property.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Pennsylvania commercial entity, nonprofit, or other organization seeking financing for a qualifying project.
Propose a project that reduces energy consumption, produces renewable energy, or replaces a dirtier fuel source.
Submit the financing application and required application fee.
Provide the requested tax returns or accountant-prepared financial statements, debt schedule, organizational documents, current financial information, and detailed project proposal.
Pass project eligibility, credit, repayment, and other underwriting review and execute the approved financing documents.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current Sustainable Energy Fund financing program accepts qualifying Pennsylvania energy projects, but approval depends on borrower finances, repayment capacity, project quality, underwriting, and negotiated loan terms rather than measure eligibility alone.
reviews.evidenceText: The current Sustainable Energy Fund financing page covers Pennsylvania commercial and nonprofit energy projects and requires an application fee, project proposal, historical and current financial records, debt information, entity documents, and credit underwriting.

approvalRequirements: Have an eligible commercial, institutional, or multifamily project at a District of Columbia property.
Use a currently qualifying product or measure and satisfy the applicable equipment and customer rules.
Obtain DCSEU preapproval before purchase for standard HVAC, refrigeration, and other projects where the current pathway requires it.
For instant lighting, purchase qualifying products through a participating distributor and identify the eligible District project at the point of sale.
Submit the required application, invoices, specifications, photographs, and installation records and allow post-installation verification.
Comply with current location-level incentive caps and program funding limits.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: DCSEU publishes current prescriptive and instant rebate pathways with objective product, preapproval, documentation, and verification rules. A qualifying preapproved project or valid instant-lighting purchase is likely to receive the incentive within program caps and available funds.
reviews.evidenceText: Current DCSEU pages require preapproval before purchase for standard HVAC and refrigeration projects, provide point-of-sale instant lighting through participating distributors, require project documentation and verification, and impose current incentive caps.
